method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::defau: Extracts the HIR `Defaultness` of a local item, impl item, or trait item by calling `hir_node_by_def_id` and matching the returned node shape.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::adt_s: Computes the `Sized`-relevant tail constraint for a struct ADT, rejecting infinitely recursive locals, non-structs, missing tails, error types, and explicit `Sized` bounds that already prove the tail is sized. It calls `representability`, `adt_def`, `non_enum_variant`, `tail_opt`, `type_of`, `instantiate_identity`, and then `sized_constraint_for_ty`; afterward it calls `references_error`, `require_lang_item`, and `predicates_of` to suppress redundant constraints before returning a bound result.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::param: Builds and normalizes the parameter environment for `def_id` from its instantiated predicates, adding extra RPITIT projection predicates for default trait methods before normalization. It calls `predicates_of` and `instantiate_identity` to get the initial predicates; for eligible associated trait fns it calls `def_kind`, `associated_item`, `defaultness`, `has_value`, `fn_sig`, and `visit_with` on `ImplTraitInTraitFinder`; finally it calls `as_local`, `mk_clauses`, `new`, `def_span`, `misc`, and `normalize_param_env_or_error` to produce the normalized `ParamEnv`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::impl<: Tracks binder nesting while visiting by shifting the stored depth inward, calling `super_visit_with` on the binder contents, then shifting the depth back outward with `shift_out`.

Finds RPITIT projection aliases belonging to the current function, adds a projection predicate equating each alias to its default/opaque type, and recursively visits the alias bounds. When it matches a fresh relevant alias, it calls `opt_rpitit_info`, `insert`, `fold_regions`, `type_of`, `instantiate`, `push`, `bind_with_vars`, and `to_predicate`; then it calls `item_bounds`, `iter_instantiated`, and `visit_with` to continue walking nested bounds, otherwise it falls back to `super_visit_with`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::param: Returns the parameter environment for `def_id` in reveal-all mode by calling `param_env` and then `with_reveal_all_normalized` on the result.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::issue: Detects the special marker-trait impl shape used by the issue-33140 trait-object compatibility hack and returns the impl self type when it matches. It calls `impl_trait_header`, `unwrap_or_else`, and `skip_binder` to inspect the impl, then uses `associated_item_def_ids` and `predicates_of` to require a marker-like, predicate-free impl, and finally calls `self_ty` and inspects `kind`, `is_static`, and `principal` before returning `bind(self_ty)` on success.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::async: Computes whether a local item is async by calling `hir_node_by_def_id`, obtaining its optional `fn_sig`, and using `map_or` to translate the HIR asyncness flag into `ty::Asyncness`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::unsiz: Computes which generic type or const parameters of an ADT can participate in structural unsizing by collecting parameters mentioned in the last field and removing any also mentioned in earlier fields. It calls `adt_def`, `generics_of`, and `count` to size the result set, then uses `non_enum_variant`, `split_last`, `new_empty`, `type_of`, `instantiate_identity`, and `walk`, inserting or removing indices based on the scanned field arguments.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/ty.rs::provi: Registers this module's query provider functions by overwriting the corresponding entries in `Providers` with `asyncness`, `adt_sized_constraint`, `param_env`, `param_env_reveal_all_normalized`, `issue33140_self_ty`, `defaultness`, and `unsizing_params_for_adt`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Sets the candidate set to `ProjectionCandidateSet::Ambiguous`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Sets the candidate set to `ProjectionCandidateSet::Error(err)` to record a selection failure; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Adds a projection candidate when possible, deduplicates identical candidates, prefers `ParamEnv` candidates over others, and otherwise converts a conflicting single candidate into ambiguity. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Handles higher-ranked projection equality by instantiating the obligation binder with placeholders inside a probe and then calling `project_and_unify_type`. It converts mismatches into `MismatchedProjectionTypes` and, when experimenting with extended GATs, filters out obligations that mention the newly created universe before returning `Holds`.

Solves a concrete projection equality by first calling `opt_normalize_projection_type` to normalize the projection, then replacing opaque types in the expected term with inference variables, and finally equating the normalized and expected terms. It returns `Holds` with accumulated obligations on success, or reports failed normalization, recursion, or mismatched projection types.

Public entry point that normalizes an associated-type projection to a `Term`. It explicitly calls `opt_normalize_projection_type`; if that returns no concrete result due to ambiguity, it falls back to `infer_projection` to create an inference variable and deferred obligations.

Attempts to normalize a projection type with recursion detection and projection-cache support, returning either a concrete normalized term, ambiguity, or in-progress recursion. It explicitly calls `project` to compute the projection when cache lookup does not decide the result, and then records progress, ambiguity, or errors back into the cache while extending the caller's obligations.

Produces an error-tolerant normalized term by creating a fresh type or const inference variable and adding the projected trait obligation so trait solving can continue. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Normalizes an inherent associated type by checking recursion depth, computing impl arguments, adding instantiated predicates as obligations, and normalizing the resulting type if it still contains aliases. It calls `compute_inherent_assoc_ty_args`.

Infers the impl arguments for an inherent associated type by freshening the parent impl args, normalizing the impl self type and projection self type when needed, and equating them before rebasing the alias arguments onto the impl. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Constructs a `Progress` value whose term is an error type and whose obligations list is empty; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Appends additional obligations to an existing `Progress` result and returns it; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Top-level projection solver that checks recursion and prior errors, assembles candidates from the parameter environment, trait definition, object bounds, and impl selection, then either confirms a unique candidate or returns ambiguity/error/no-progress. It calls `assemble_candidates_from_param_env`, `assemble_candidates_from_trait_def`, `assemble_candidates_from_object_ty`, `assemble_candidates_from_impls`, `confirm_candidate`, `Progress::error`, and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`/`ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_error` indirectly through candidate assembly outcomes.
Collects projection candidates from the caller bounds in the parameter environment. It calls `assemble_candidates_from_predicates`.

Scans item bounds from the trait definition for matching projection clauses, pushes matching trait-definition candidates, and marks ambiguity when matching cannot be decided. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::push_candidate` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`.

Builds projection candidates from object type projection bounds when the trait supports object-based projection, and marks ambiguity if the self type is still a type variable. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous` and `assemble_candidates_from_predicates`.

Filters a stream of projection predicates by associated item and argument compatibility, probes whether each can match the goal, and either pushes a candidate or marks ambiguity. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::push_candidate` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`.

Selects the underlying trait obligation to derive impl-based projection candidates, then records ambiguity, selection error, or a usable builtin/user-defined candidate while accounting for specialization and builtin trait cases. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_error`.

Turns a chosen projection candidate into concrete projected progress by delegating to the appropriate confirmation routine and then opportunistically resolving inferred regions in the resulting term. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` for `ParamEnv`, `Object`, and `TraitDef` candidates, and `confirm_select_candidate` for `Select` candidates.

Confirms an impl-selected candidate by dispatching to the appropriate builtin or user-defined confirmation path based on the selected impl source and trait kind. It calls `confirm_impl_candidate`, `confirm_coroutine_candidate`, `confirm_future_candidate`, `confirm_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_async_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_closure_candidate`, `confirm_fn_pointer_candidate`, `confirm_async_closure_candidate`, `confirm_async_fn_kind_helper_candidate`, and `confirm_builtin_candidate`.

Computes the projected `Coroutine` associated type (`Yield` or `Return`) from the normalized coroutine signature and confirms it as if it came from an environment projection. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Computes the `Future::Output` projection from the normalized coroutine signature of an async future and confirms it through the param-env projection path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Computes the `Iterator::Item` projection from the normalized coroutine signature of a generator and confirms it through the param-env projection path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Computes the `AsyncIterator::Item` projection by normalizing the coroutine signature, extracting the yielded `Poll<Option<Item>>` structure, and confirming the resulting item type through the param-env path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Resolves built-in associated type projections such as discriminant, async destructor, or pointee metadata, building any extra obligations needed, then confirms the resulting projection through the param-env path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.
Normalizes a function pointer signature and confirms its callable output projection via the shared callable path. It calls `confirm_callable_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Builds the effective callable signature for closures or coroutine-closures, including async/coroutine-specific output construction when needed, then confirms the resulting callable projection. It calls `confirm_callable_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.
Constructs the `FnOnce::Output` projection predicate from a callable signature and confirms it through the param-env projection path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate`.

Computes the projected future type for async callable traits by analyzing coroutine-closure, closure, or function-like self types and then confirming the resulting projection predicate. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate`.

Computes the helper projection that derives tupled upvars for a requested async closure kind and confirms it as a param-env style projection. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Confirms a projection candidate taken from the parameter environment by instantiating the cached binder, normalizing the obligation projection and optionally the candidate projection with `normalize_with_depth_to`, equating the two projections via inference, and on success extending obligations and calling `assoc_ty_own_obligations`; on failure it returns an error term.

Confirms a projection candidate coming from a selected impl by locating the associated item in the impl, rebasing and translating trait/impl arguments, building the resulting associated term from the impl item definition, checking argument compatibility, and then calling `assoc_ty_own_obligations` before instantiating the term; if the impl item is missing or incompatible it returns an error progress.

Collects and adds the associated item's own declared predicates as nested obligations by instantiating the item's predicates, normalizing each predicate with `normalize_with_depth_to`, choosing an appropriate obligation cause, and pushing each normalized predicate as a deeper obligation.
Trait method contract for deriving a projection-cache key from a poly projection predicate and selection context.

Builds a `ProjectionCacheKey` for a poly projection predicate only when it has no bound vars. It explicitly calls `ProjectionCacheKey::new` after resolving inference variables in the predicate's projection type with `resolve_vars_if_possible`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/check/wf: Returns the underlying `ObligationCtxt` by dereferencing `WfCheckingCtxt`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context inside the obligation context; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Normalizes a type-foldable value under the current parameter environment, attaching a `WellFormed` obligation cause for diagnostics; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Builds and registers a `WellFormed` predicate obligation for a generic argument using the current body and parameter environment. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`.

Creates the temporary inference/obligation context used for well-formedness checking, runs the supplied checker closure, solves obligations, computes implied bounds, lints redundant lifetimes, and resolves/report regions with a compatibility path for some implied-bounds cases; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Top-level dispatcher that selects the appropriate WF checker for the HIR node kind and then checks each generic parameter. It calls `check_item`, `check_trait_item`, `check_impl_item`, `check_foreign_item`, `check_item_type`, and `check_param_wf`.

Checks item-level well-formedness after precollecting item types, handling impls, functions, statics/consts/type aliases, ADTs, and traits according to item kind. It calls `check_impl`, `check_item_fn`, `check_item_type`, `check_type_defn`, and `check_trait`.
Checks a foreign item after precollecting its type information, validating foreign functions and statics while accepting foreign types unchanged. It calls `check_item_fn` and `check_item_type`.

Checks a trait item by precollecting its types, diagnosing misuse of the trait name as an unboxed self trait object, validating the associated item itself, and also validating synthesized associated types for RPITIT methods. It calls `check_dyn_incompatible_self_trait_by_name` and `check_associated_item`.

Analyzes generic associated types across all associated items of a trait to infer potentially missing outlives bounds by repeatedly intersecting constraints discovered from method signatures and other bounds. It calls `gather_gat_bounds`, `augment_param_env`, `region_known_to_outlive`, and `ty_known_to_outlive`.

Extends a parameter environment with additional clause predicates, returning the original environment unchanged when no new predicates are provided; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Collects GAT arguments appearing in a type/signature and derives required outlives clauses by checking whether referenced types or regions are known to outlive each region argument. It calls `GATArgsCollector::visit`, `ty_known_to_outlive`, and `region_known_to_outlive`.
Tests whether a type is known to outlive a region under the current environment by creating a region obligation probe. It calls `test_region_obligations`.
Tests whether one region is known to outlive another under the current environment by probing a subregion constraint. It calls `test_region_obligations`.

Creates a fresh inference context, applies a caller-provided set of region constraints, derives implied bounds from assumed well-formed types, and returns whether region solving succeeds without errors; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Constructs a `GATArgsCollector`, walks a type-foldable value, and returns the non-bound region and type arguments used at the target GAT projection. It calls `GATArgsCollector::visit_ty` indirectly through the visitor traversal.
Visitor hook that records lifetime and type arguments from projections of the targeted GAT, then continues recursively through nested types; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Returns whether a HIR type syntactically looks like a single-segment trait object naming the enclosing trait, indicating it may have meant `Self`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Checks whether a trait item mistakenly refers to its own trait name where `Self` is intended, and emits a suggestion-based diagnostic when this makes the trait non-object-safe. It calls `could_be_self` to detect suspicious type references in associated const/type/function signatures and calls `is_object_safe` to skip diagnostics for object-safe traits.

Checks an impl item after precollecting its types, choosing an appropriate diagnostic span for methods and associated types before delegating to associated-item WF checking. It calls `check_associated_item`.

Checks generic-parameter well-formedness, focusing on const parameters: it either enforces the relevant lang-item trait bound in a WF context on feature-enabled paths or emits structural-match style diagnostics on stable paths. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt` and contains the local helper `ty_is_local`.
Local helper used by `check_param_wf` to decide whether a const-parameter type is local by recursively inspecting ADTs, arrays, slices, shared references, and tuples. It calls itself recursively.

Runs WF checking for an associated const, function, or type inside a dedicated context, ensuring trait coherence first, computing the appropriate `Self` type, and then validating the item-specific signature or value/type. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_associated_type_bounds`.

Checks structs, unions, and enums for representability and field/type well-formedness, enforces `Sized` where required for non-tail fields or packed/drop-sensitive layouts, registers extra obligations such as const evaluatability, and validates where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks a trait item by rejecting associated items on marker traits, validating the trait's where-clauses in a WF context, and then running the GAT missing-bound analysis for real traits. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `check_where_clauses`, and `check_gat_where_clauses`.

Validates explicit bounds on a trait associated type by normalizing each bound, expanding it into clause well-formedness obligations, and registering those obligations. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx` and `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`.
Checks a free or foreign function signature inside a dedicated WF context using the instantiated function signature. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`.

Checks the declared type of an item in a WF context by normalizing it, registering its well-formedness, optionally enforcing `Sized` depending on unsized-handling rules, and requiring `Sync` for eligible shared statics. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.

Checks an impl in a WF context by validating either the implemented trait reference and its derived obligations or the inherent self type, then validating the impl's where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks where-clauses and generic defaults for well-formedness by registering obligations for concrete default types/consts, examining predicate dependencies, normalizing predicates, and feeding the resulting obligations into the current WF context. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.
Visits a type, records the index of any `ty::Param` encountered in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.
Stops traversal when a region is encountered by immediately returning `ControlFlow::Break(())`; it does not call other methods from the list.
Visits a const, records the index of any const generic parameter found in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.

Well-formedness-checks a function or method signature by liberating late-bound regions, normalizing each input/output type with per-parameter locations, registering WF obligations for every input/output type, and checking where-clauses. It explicitly calls `check_where_clauses` and uses `register_bound` to enforce the tuple and `Sized` requirements for `Abi::RustCall` arguments.

Validates a method's `self` receiver by normalizing the method signature, `self_ty`, and receiver type, then checking receiver legality. It explicitly calls `receiver_is_valid`, potentially multiple times under different feature configurations, to decide whether the receiver is accepted or which diagnostic to emit.

Emits error E0307 for an invalid `self` parameter type, adding an explanatory note and help text before returning the emitted diagnostic. It directly calls `dcx`, `with_note`, `with_help`, and `emit`.

Determines whether a method receiver type is valid for a given `Self` type by first trying direct type equality, then autodereferencing toward `self_ty`, registering autoderef obligations on success. When arbitrary self types are not enabled, it explicitly calls `receiver_is_implemented` at each deref step and also registers the corresponding `Receiver` bound before continuing.

Checks whether a candidate receiver type satisfies the `Receiver` lang-item trait by building the trait obligation and testing it with `predicate_must_hold_modulo_regions`; it does not call other methods from the list.

Checks that generic parameters of an ADT or lazy type alias are sufficiently constrained for variance computation, skipping items whose field/alias types already contain errors. It explicitly calls `identify_constrained_generic_params` to extend the constrained set and `report_bivariance` to emit diagnostics for unconstrained parameters.

Builds and emits the diagnostic for an unused/bivariant generic parameter, selecting item-specific help text and collecting spans where the parameter or `Self` alias appears. It explicitly calls `IsProbablyCyclical::visit_def` to detect likely recursive ADTs/type aliases so it can report recursive-usage diagnostics instead of plain unused-parameter errors.

Finds elaborated predicates on the current item that are globally true but nontrivial, normalizes them, refines their source span to the matching predicate clause when possible, and registers them as `TrivialBound` obligations. It does not call other methods from the provided list.

Runs well-formedness checking over all items, impl items, trait items, foreign items, and opaques in a module in parallel, combining their results, and checks for the crate entry function at the crate root. It explicitly calls `check_well_formed` for each covered definition.
Registers this module's query providers by installing `check_mod_type_wf` and `check_well_formed` into the compiler provider table. It explicitly references `check_mod_type_wf` from the methods list.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Builds the full predicate set for a definition by starting from `tcx.predicates_defined_on(def_id)` and, for trait definitions, appending the implicit `Self: Trait` predicate via `ty::TraitRef::identity(...).upcast(...)`.

Collects explicit predicates written on a local item, with special inheritance/rebasing paths for RPITITs and normal HIR lowering otherwise. For RPITIT trait items, it calls `tcx.explicit_predicates_of(...)` to inherit parent function predicates and `compute_bidirectional_outlives_predicates(...)` to add duplicated lifetime equalities. For RPITIT impl items, it calls `tcx.explicit_predicates_of(...)` again and rebases those trait associated-item predicates onto the impl. In the general path, it lowers item generics, bounds, implicit `Sized`/const-arg predicates, and default-impl/delegation-related predicates into `ty::GenericPredicates`.

Adds paired outlives predicates equating each duplicated opaque lifetime parameter with its original parent lifetime. It calls `tcx.map_opaque_lifetime_to_parent_lifetime(...)` to find the original lifetime and pushes two `RegionOutlives` clauses for both directions.

Traverses the HIR for an item to collect `ConstEvaluatable` predicates for unevaluated anonymous consts appearing in impl headers, generics, and function signatures. It drives the visitor by calling `visit_trait_ref(...)`, `visit_ty(...)`, `visit_generics(...)`, and `visit_fn_decl(...)`, while relying on `visit_anon_const(...)` to record predicates and `visit_const_param_default(...)` to skip const parameter defaults.

Visitor hook that turns an unevaluated anonymous const into a `ConstEvaluatable` clause. It calls `ty::Const::from_anon_const(...)` to lower the const and inserts the predicate when the resulting const kind is unevaluated.
Visitor hook that intentionally ignores const parameter defaults so they are checked only when instantiated; it does not call any other methods in this file.
Trait-only wrapper that asserts the definition is a trait and then calls `gather_explicit_predicates_of(...)` to collect its explicit predicates and bounds.

Computes the user-visible explicit predicates for a local item. For traits, it calls `trait_explicit_predicates_and_bounds(...)` and filters out associated-type bounds that should instead be reported through item bounds. For other items, it ultimately calls `gather_explicit_predicates_of(...)`, with extra handling to inherit predicates for anon const defaults and to append const-parameter type predicates where needed.
Returns only the immediate supertrait predicates for a trait by calling `implied_predicates_with_filter(...)` with `PredicateFilter::SelfOnly`.
Returns supertrait predicates whose `Self` bounds may define a named associated item by calling `implied_predicates_with_filter(...)` with `PredicateFilter::SelfThatDefines(assoc_name)`.

Computes the implied predicates for a trait or trait alias by calling `implied_predicates_with_filter(...)` with `PredicateFilter::All` for trait aliases and `PredicateFilter::SelfAndAssociatedTypeBounds` for ordinary traits.

Lowers a trait’s supertrait list and matching where-clause bounds into implied predicates according to the requested filter. For external traits it calls `tcx.super_predicates_of(...)`; for local traits it calls `icx.lowerer().lower_mono_bounds(...)` and `icx.probe_ty_param_bounds_in_generics(...)` to gather bounds, then recursively forces `tcx.super_predicates_of(...)` or `tcx.implied_predicates_of(...)` on positive trait bounds to detect cycles and elaborate nested associated-type bounds.

Collects predicates relevant to a specific type parameter within an item, including inherited parent bounds, local where-clause bounds, and the implicit `Self: Trait` bound for trait `Self`. It calls `ItemCtxt::probe_ty_param_bounds(...)` on the parent when needed and `ItemCtxt::probe_ty_param_bounds_in_generics(...)` on the current item, then filters the result to trait predicates whose self type is the target parameter.

Collects lowered predicate clauses for a specific type parameter from the HIR generics where-clause, honoring the requested `PredicateFilter` to keep all bounds, only `Self` bounds, or only `Self` bounds that define a particular associated item. It iterates bound predicates, chooses the bounded type either from the target parameter or by lowering the predicate’s explicit bounded type, lowers matching bounds into a `Bounds` accumulator, and returns the accumulated clauses with spans. This method explicitly calls `is_param_bound`, `to_def_id`, `to_ty`, `late_bound_vars`, `astconv`, `add_bounds`, `map_or`, `bound_defines_assoc_item`, and `clauses`.

Checks whether a trait bound could define a particular associated item name. It calls `trait_ref.trait_def_id()` to resolve the bound’s trait and then `self.tcx.trait_may_define_assoc_item(...)` to test that trait.
Constructs an early-bound `ResolvedArg` for a generic parameter and returns it paired with the parameter's local def-id; it calls `to_def_id` to convert the local id for `ResolvedArg::EarlyBound`.

Constructs an innermost late-bound `ResolvedArg` for a generic parameter at the given index and returns it paired with the parameter's local def-id; it calls `to_def_id` to build `ResolvedArg::LateBound`.
Returns the underlying `DefId` for early-bound, late-bound, and free resolved arguments, and `None` for `StaticLifetime` or `Error`; it does not call other methods from the list.
Shifts the De Bruijn depth of a late-bound argument by the given amount and leaves other variants unchanged; for `ResolvedArg::LateBound` it calls `shifted_in` on the depth.
Formats each `Scope` variant in a truncated debug form that omits recursive scope tails; it calls the formatter builder methods `debug_struct`, `field`, and `finish`.

Registers this module's query providers, wiring `resolve_bound_vars`, `is_late_bound_map`, `object_lifetime_default`, and closure-based accessors for stored maps; the accessors call `tcx.resolve_bound_vars(id)` and then `get` on the resulting maps.

Builds the `ResolveBoundVars` result for one HIR owner by creating a `BoundVarContext`, dispatching to the matching visitor entry point, and then copying collected definitions into owner-indexed maps. It calls `hir_owner_node`, then one of `visit_item`, `visit_foreign_item`, `visit_trait_item`, or `visit_impl_item`, and finally uses `entry`, `or_default`, and `insert` to populate the result.

Converts a `ResolvedArg::LateBound` plus its generic parameter into the corresponding `ty::BoundVariableKind`, using the parameter kind to choose region, type, or const binding. It calls `hir`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `expect_local`, and `name` to recover the bound variable's HIR name.

Walks outward through the current scope stack to determine the binder variables and binder composition mode for a nested poly-trait-ref, including concatenating enclosing binder vars with supertrait vars when needed. It calls `clone`, `is_empty`, `dcx`, `delayed_bug`, `entry`, `or_default`, and `extend`.

Processes a poly trait reference by computing enclosing binder context, creating late-bound entries for its bound generic parameters, optionally rejecting non-lifetime binders, recording the resulting binder list, and visiting the trait ref inside a new binder scope. It calls `poly_trait_ref_binder_info`, `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `insert`, `extend`, `deny_non_region_late_bound`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, and `visit_trait_ref`.
Returns the HIR map used for nested visiting; it calls `hir` on the type context.
Visits a nested body within a `Body` scope so inner references resolve with the body boundary in place. It calls `hir`, `body`, `with`, `id`, and `visit_body`.

Handles closure expressions specially: it diagnoses inferred types inside `for<>` closures, builds late-bound vars for closure binders, rejects non-region late-bound params, records the binders, and then visits the closure within a new binder scope; non-closure expressions are walked normally. It calls the local helper `span_of_infer`, then `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `deny_non_region_late_bound`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, and `walk_expr`.
Local helper for `visit_expr` that searches a type for an inferred `_` and returns its span if found. It calls the nested visitor's `visit_ty` and then `break_value` on the control-flow result.
Searches a type subtree for the first inferred type and stores its span, otherwise continues traversal. It calls `is_some` to stop after a hit and `walk_ty` to recurse into nested types.

Dispatches item handling based on item kind: records empty late-bound vars for trait impl refs, uses `visit_early_late` for functions, walks items with no lifetime parameters directly, gives opaque types a parent-aware root plus binder and trait-ref-boundary scopes, and uses early-binding handling for other generic items. It calls `record_late_bound_vars`, `visit_early_late`, `walk_item`, `ResolvedArg::early`, `insert`, `with`, and `visit_early`.
Handles foreign items by using `visit_early_late` for foreign functions and otherwise just walking foreign statics and types. It calls `visit_early_late` and `walk_foreign_item`.

Resolves bindings inside types, with special handling for bare function types, trait objects, explicit lifetime parameters, references, and opaque defs. It builds and records late-bound vars for bare fns, visits trait-object bounds under a trait-ref boundary, applies object lifetime defaulting or normal lifetime visiting, and performs additional opaque-type validation. It calls `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `deny_non_region_late_bound`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, `walk_ty`, `visit_poly_trait_ref_inner`, `resolve_object_lifetime_default`, and `visit_lifetime`.

Handles trait items by using `visit_early_late` for methods, `visit_early` plus explicit traversal for associated types, and `visit_early` plus normal walking for associated consts. It calls `visit_early_late`, `walk_trait_item`, `visit_early`, `visit_generics`, `visit_param_bound`, and `visit_ty`.

Handles impl items by using `visit_early_late` for methods, `visit_early` plus explicit traversal for associated types, and `visit_early` plus normal walking for associated consts. It calls `visit_early_late`, `walk_impl_item`, `visit_early`, `visit_generics`, and `visit_ty`.

Resolves a lifetime reference according to its kind: inserts `'static`, resolves named lifetime params, and ignores error or inference/default placeholders for later stages. It calls `insert_lifetime` for `Static` and `resolve_lifetime_ref` for `Param`.

Visits each path segment's generic arguments with the correct depth and resolves paths that refer to type or const parameters. It calls `visit_segment_args` for segment arguments and `resolve_type_ref` on type/const parameter paths.

Processes a function-like item by extracting the output type, copying inferred-delegation late-bound vars when present, applying lifetime elision analysis, walking the function signature/kind, and then visiting the body. It calls `fn_sig`, `skip_binder`, `bound_vars`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `visit_fn_like_elision`, `walk_fn_kind`, and `visit_nested_body`.
Visits generic parameters and where predicates inside a trait-ref-boundary scope so nested trait refs are resolved with the proper boundary. It calls `with`.

Resolves where-predicates by creating a binder scope for bound predicates, recording their late-bound vars, and then visiting the bounded type and bounds; region predicates visit the lifetime and bounds, while equality predicates visit both sides. It calls `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, `visit_ty`, and `visit_lifetime`.
Visits a poly trait ref using the general inner handler with non-lifetime binders allowed; it calls `visit_poly_trait_ref_inner`.
Visits an anonymous const under a late-boundary scope so late-bound regions cannot escape into constants. It calls `with` and `walk_anon_const`.

Resolves type and const generic parameters as references to themselves, then visits any default type, const type, or const default body attached to the parameter. It calls `resolve_type_ref`, `visit_ty`, `hir`, `body`, and `visit_body`.

Computes the object lifetime default for a type parameter by inspecting its HIR generics and collecting direct `T: 'a` outlives bounds. It queries HIR/generics metadata via `hir_node_by_def_id`, `local_parent`, `hir`, `get_generics`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, and `bounds_for_param`, and returns `Empty`, `Static`, `Param`, or `Ambiguous` depending on the collected lifetime set.
Creates a nested `BoundVarContext` with a replacement scope and executes a callback inside that scope. It enters a debug span with `enter` and then invokes the provided closure `f`.
Stores the late-bound variable binder list for a HIR node in the output map and rejects accidental overwrites. It updates the map with `insert`.

Builds a binder scope where lifetime params may be early- or late-bound depending on `tcx.is_late_bound`, records the resulting late-bound binder kinds, and visits the nested item in that scope. It calls `record_late_bound_vars` to save binder info and `with` to traverse under the constructed `Scope::Binder`.

Builds a binder scope where all generic parameters are treated as early-bound, records that there are no late-bound vars, and then visits the nested item under both a binder scope and a trait-ref boundary. It calls `record_late_bound_vars` and uses `with` twice to install the scopes.

Resolves a lifetime reference by walking outward through the scope stack, tracking De Bruijn depth, root generics, binder entries, body ownership, and late-bound capture barriers to classify the reference as early-bound, late-bound, free, error, or unresolved. It uses `generics_of`, `param_def_id_to_index`, `get_generics`, and `shifted` while traversing scopes, and emits diagnostics through `feature_err`, `emit`, and `emit_err` when fresh/elided or improperly captured lifetimes are encountered.

Resolves a type or const generic parameter reference by walking outward through scopes, tracking binder depth and late-bound capture barriers, and classifying the reference as early-bound, late-bound, or unresolved/error. It uses `generics_of`, `param_def_id_to_index`, and `shifted` during lookup, and emits capture diagnostics with `emit_err` before recording the final result with `insert`.

Visits generic arguments on a path segment, resolving explicit lifetimes first, handling paren-sugar function traits specially, and computing object-lifetime-default scopes for type arguments based on the referenced item and surrounding context. It explicitly calls `visit_fn_like_elision` for paren-sugar segments, `visit_lifetime` for lifetime args, `object_lifetime_default` to compute defaults for type parameters, `with` to enter object-default scopes, `visit_ty` for type args, `visit_anon_const` for const args, `visit_id` for inferred args, and `supertrait_hrtb_vars` when collecting higher-ranked vars from supertraits.

Searches a trait/supertrait graph for an associated item with the given name and kind, accumulating higher-ranked bound variables introduced by traversed supertrait predicates. It queries associated items with `associated_items`/`find_by_name_and_kind`, fetches relevant supertrait predicates with `super_predicates_that_define_assoc_item`, and extends the traversal stack with collected obligations.

Visits function-like input/output types under an object-lifetime-default scope that supplies `'static` for elided trait-object lifetimes, except that closure outputs are visited outside that scope. It calls `with` to install the defaulting scope and `visit_ty` to traverse input and output types.

Resolves an elided object lifetime by scanning outward for the nearest applicable object-lifetime-default scope, adjusting for intervening binders, and defaulting to `'static` at the root. It calls `insert_lifetime` to record the chosen lifetime after applying `shifted`.
Records the resolved lifetime for a lifetime HIR node in the output map. It updates the definitions table with `insert`.

Removes a previously inserted lifetime mapping when later validation determines that the resolution was erroneous, asserting that the removed value matches the expected bad definition. It removes the entry with `swap_remove`.

Computes the set of lifetime parameters in a function owner that should be treated as late-bound by comparing where each lifetime appears in inputs, outputs, and where-clauses, while excluding lifetimes constrained through type aliases after lowering. It drives analysis by calling HIR accessors such as `fn_decl_by_hir_id` and `get_generics`, invokes the nested collectors via `visit_ty`, `walk_fn_ret_ty`, and `visit_generics`, and finally allocates the resulting set with `alloc`.

Marks parameter types as constrained, skips descending into projection or inherent aliases, and otherwise continues recursive type traversal. It calls `kind` to inspect the type and `super_visit_with` to visit nested structure when traversal continues.
Ignores constants for constrained-argument collection and immediately continues traversal. It does not call other methods from the provided methods list.
Marks early-bound regions as constrained and otherwise leaves region handling unchanged. It calls `kind` to inspect the region kind.

Traverses HIR types to collect only those lifetime occurrences that contribute to input constraints, skipping associated type projections and selectively recursing into type-alias arguments based on a lowered-type constraint analysis. It calls the nested post-lowering visitor's `visit_ty`, visits constrained alias args with `visit_generic_arg`, traverses plain path segments with `visit_path_segment`, and falls back to `walk_ty` for ordinary recursive HIR traversal.
Collects named lifetime parameters encountered by the constrained-input visitor into its region set. It does not call any other methods from the methods list.
Collects every named lifetime parameter encountered during traversal into its region set. It does not call any other methods from the methods list.

Rejects late-bound type or const parameters in a binder, emitting either an immediate feature-gated error or a delayed bug, and rewrites their recorded resolution to `Error`. It queries the parameter node with `hir_node_by_def_id` and emits diagnostics through `struct_span_err`, `emit`, and `delay_as_bug`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Normalizes a value under the old trait solver and returns any generated obligations. If `next_trait_solver` is enabled it returns the input unchanged with empty obligations; otherwise it creates a `SelectionContext` with `new`, clones the obligation cause with `clone`, and calls `normalize_with_depth`.

Performs full normalization and obligation fulfillment. If `next_trait_solver` is enabled it calls the new-solver `deeply_normalize`; otherwise it calls `normalize`, registers obligations via `into_value_registering_obligations`, drives fulfillment with `select_where_possible`, resolves inference variables with `resolve_vars_if_possible`, and checks `is_empty` to return either the normalized value or collected errors.

Entry point that normalizes a value while tracking recursion depth and collecting obligations into a fresh buffer. It creates the obligation list with `new` and delegates the actual work to `normalize_with_depth_to`.
Runs normalization into an existing obligation buffer. It constructs an `AssocTypeNormalizer` with `new` and then normalizes by calling `AssocTypeNormalizer::fold` inside `ensure_sufficient_stack`.

Fast pre-check for whether a value may contain aliases that require normalization. It queries the typing mode with `typing_mode`, removes opaque-type flags with `remove` when opaques are rigid, and finally tests the remaining flags with `has_type_flags`.

Constructs an `AssocTypeNormalizer` for old-solver normalization, initializing its context, recursion depth, obligation sink, and universe stack. It debug-checks that `next_trait_solver` is not active.

Top-level fold helper that first resolves inference variables with `resolve_vars_if_possible`, rejects escaping bound variables, checks `needs_normalization`, and if needed recursively normalizes by calling `fold_with`.
Returns the type context used by the folder by delegating to the selection context; it calls `tcx` on `self.selcx`.
Normalizes inside a binder while tracking universe state. It pushes a new universe marker with `push`, recursively folds the binder contents with `super_fold_with`, and restores the stack with `pop`.

Core type-normalization routine for aliases. It first checks `needs_normalization`; non-alias types are recursively handled with `super_fold_with`. For opaque aliases it consults `typing_mode`, gets the folder context via `cx`, checks the recursion limit with `recursion_limit` and `value_within_limit`, reports overflow with `err_ctxt` and `report_overflow_error`, and then expands and recursively normalizes the revealed type using `type_of`, `instantiate`, and `fold_with`. For projection aliases it may recurse into arguments with `super_fold_with`, inspect escaping binders with `has_escaping_bound_vars`, normalize directly with `normalize_projection_ty`, or use bound-variable replacement helpers such as `replace_bound_vars`, `opt_normalize_projection_term`, `replace_placeholders`, and `fold_with` to safely attempt projection under binders, while extending obligations and associated item predicates as needed.

Normalizes constants when generic const expressions are not enabled and the constant still `needs_normalization`. It obtains the type context with `tcx`, recursively folds substructure with `super_fold_with`, then calls `with_replaced_escaping_bound_vars` to evaluate the const through `evaluate_const`, and finally folds the result again with `super_fold_with`.

Normalizes a predicate only when the predicate `allow_normalization` and `needs_normalization` both hold; in that case it recursively normalizes by calling `super_fold_with`, otherwise it leaves the predicate unchanged.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/astconv/: Scans explicit bounds and relevant where-clause predicates for relaxed `?Trait` bounds, diagnoses multiple relaxed default bounds, warns for non-`?Sized` relaxations, and injects the implicit `Sized` bound when no `?Sized` was provided and the lang item exists. This method calls the local helper closure `search_bounds` to collect `?Trait` bounds, and uses `bounds.push_sized` to add the implicit `Sized` predicate.

Lowers each HIR generic bound on a type parameter into internal predicates in `Bounds`: trait bounds become instantiated trait predicates, lang-item trait bounds become instantiated lang-item trait predicates, and lifetime bounds become outlives predicates. This method calls `instantiate_poly_trait_ref` for ordinary trait bounds, `instantiate_lang_item_trait_ref` for lang-item trait bounds, `ast_region_to_region` to lower lifetime syntax, and `bounds.push_region_bound` to record outlives predicates.

Builds a fresh `Bounds` set for a parameter by choosing whether only self-bounds should be kept, filtering the input HIR bounds according to the requested `PredicateFilter`, and then lowering the surviving bounds. This method calls `add_bounds` to perform the actual lowering after applying the filter.

Resolves an associated type or return-type-notation binding against the current trait or an appropriate supertrait, checks visibility/stability and duplicate bindings, and then adds the resulting equality or constraint predicates to `Bounds` for the selected associated item. This method calls `trait_defines_associated_item_named` to test whether the current trait defines the named item, `one_bound_for_assoc_method` to find the unique supertrait method target for return-type notation, and `one_bound_for_assoc_type` to find the unique supertrait associated type target when the item is not defined on the current trait.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_resolve/src/late.rs::impl: Returns a fixed human-readable description string for each `PatternSource` variant; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Converts a `PatternSource` into a borrowed string diagnostic argument by calling `PatternSource::descr` and wrapping the result in `DiagnosticArgValue::Str`.
Forces the state to `Yes` when the boolean flag is true, otherwise preserves the existing `ConstantHasGenerics` value; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns the textual keyword for the constant item kind, mapping `Const` to `"const"` and `Static` to `"static"`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Classifies whether a `RibKind` represents a scope that contains generic parameters, returning `true` for assoc/item-style barriers and `false` for normal/function/module/const-param-like ribs; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Determines whether a rib kind blocks label lookup across that scope, treating most item/function-like ribs as barriers and `Normal`/`MacroDefinition` as non-barriers; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Constructs a new `Rib` with default-initialized bindings and the provided `RibKind`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns a short descriptive string for each `LifetimeBinderKind`, such as `type`, `bound`, `item`, `impl block`, `function`, or `closure`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Constructs a new `LifetimeRib` with default bindings and the supplied `LifetimeRibKind`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Maps each `PathSource` to the namespace late resolution should search, using the type namespace for type/trait/struct contexts, the value namespace for expression/pattern/tuple-struct/delegation contexts, and preserving the namespace stored in `TraitItem`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Indicates whether unresolved handling for this path source should be deferred to type checking, returning `true` for most type/value path contexts and `false` for trait, trait-item, and delegation contexts; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Produces the user-facing description of what kind of entity a path is expected to resolve to, with extra inspection for call expressions to distinguish values, functions, tuple structs/variants, and external crates; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Checks whether the path source is specifically an expression used as a call target; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Validates whether a resolved `Res` is acceptable for the given path context by matching allowed definition kinds per source. It explicitly calls `Res::expected_in_unit_struct_pat` and `Res::expected_in_tuple_struct_pat` for pattern-related cases.

Selects the appropriate resolution error code for this path context, distinguishing between missing names and names that resolved to an unexpected kind; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Evaluates whether a documented target should be treated as exported by deriving a local `DefId` or visibility-based answer from the `MaybeExported` variant, then consulting effective visibilities when needed; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Intentionally skips resolving attribute contents because attribute expressions do not correspond to executable code; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Enters item resolution by updating diagnostic state, forcing item-level error reporting, and resolving the item inside an item lifetime rib. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_item`.
Delegates match-arm handling directly to the arm resolver. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_arm`.
Resolves a block while saving and restoring the enclosing `macro_rules` scope to prevent leakage across block traversal. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_block`.
Rejects generic visitor traversal of anonymous constants and forces callers to use the dedicated anon-const resolution path instead; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Delegates expression traversal to the late expression resolver with no special parent expression context. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_expr`.
Temporarily records the current pattern for diagnostics, then performs normal pattern walking; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Captures span metadata for a non-wild local binding to improve diagnostics, then resolves the local and restores the previous let-binding context. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_local`.

Resolves type syntax with specialized handling for elided reference lifetimes, type paths, implicit `Self`, impl traits, trait objects, bare function types, arrays, const arguments, and `typeof`. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_elided_lifetime`, `LateResolutionVisitor::smart_resolve_path`, `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_path`, `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`, `LateResolutionVisitor::record_lifetime_params_for_impl_trait`, `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_generic_params`, `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_fn_signature`, and `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_anon_const`.

Resolves a higher-ranked trait reference inside a generic-parameter and lifetime binder scope, visiting bound generics before resolving and traversing the trait reference itself. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_generic_params`, `LateResolutionVisitor::smart_resolve_path`, and `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_trait_ref`.

Resolves doc links for a foreign item, then dispatches foreign type aliases and functions through generic-parameter ribs, statics through a static rib, and rejects unexpanded foreign macros. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_doc_links`.

Resolves function and closure signatures, generics, ribs, labels, parameters, return types, bodies, and coroutine/impl-trait lifetime bookkeeping, with special early handling for foreign or body-less functions. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_fn_header`, `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_generics`, `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_fn_signature`, `LateResolutionVisitor::record_lifetime_params_for_impl_trait`, `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_closure_binder`, `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_params`, `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_block`, and `LateResolutionVisitor::visit_expr`.
Delegates lifetime uses directly to the lifetime resolver. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_lifetime`.
Resolves a generics block by visiting its generic parameters and then each where-clause predicate. It explicitly calls `visit_generic_params` and `visit_where_predicate`.
Resolves a closure binder; it does nothing for `NotPresent` and, for `for<...>` binders, visits the binder's generic parameters. It explicitly calls `visit_generic_params`.

Resolves a generic argument while marking that generic arguments are being processed. For type arguments, it may reinterpret a trivial path type as a const argument by probing lexical resolution with `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`, then resolving it inside `resolve_anon_const_manual` via `smart_resolve_path` and `visit_path`; otherwise it visits the type with `visit_ty`. For lifetime arguments it calls `visit_lifetime`, and for const arguments it calls `resolve_anon_const`.

Resolves an associated-item constraint by visiting its identifier, optional generic arguments, and constraint body. It explicitly calls `visit_ident`, wraps generic arguments in `with_lifetime_rib` before calling `visit_generic_args`, uses `visit_ty` or `resolve_anon_const` for equality terms, and calls `record_lifetime_params_for_impl_trait` for bound constraints.

Resolves generic arguments attached to a path segment. For angle-bracketed arguments it delegates to `visit::walk_generic_args`; for parenthesized arguments it inspects lifetime ribs and either introduces an anonymous-lifetime rib with `with_lifetime_rib` and resolves the function-like signature via `resolve_fn_signature`, or falls back to `visit::walk_generic_args`.

Resolves a where-clause predicate while tracking it in diagnostic metadata and forbidding anonymous lifetimes by default. For bound predicates it enters `with_lifetime_rib`, then `with_generic_param_rib`, and explicitly calls `visit_generic_params`, `visit_ty`, and `visit_param_bound`; otherwise it falls back to `visit::walk_where_predicate`.

Resolves names inside an inline assembly block by walking each operand. It explicitly calls `visit_expr` for input/output expressions, `resolve_anon_const` for const operands, `visit_inline_asm_sym` for symbol operands, and `visit_block` for label operands.

Resolves an inline-asm symbol path inside dedicated value, type, and label ribs so surrounding bindings are blocked like anon-const resolution. It explicitly nests `with_rib` and `with_label_rib`, then calls `smart_resolve_path` and `visit::walk_inline_asm_sym`.
Resolves documentation links attached to an enum variant and then walks the variant body. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links` and `visit::walk_variant`.
Resolves an enum variant discriminant as an anonymous const in enum-discriminant context. It explicitly calls `resolve_anon_const`.
Resolves documentation links attached to a field definition and then walks the field. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links` and `visit::walk_field_def`.

Constructs a late-resolution visitor rooted at the crate graph root, initializing parent scope, namespace ribs, label and lifetime stacks, and diagnostic state. It explicitly calls `ParentScope::module`, `Rib::new`, and `Default::default`.
Attempts lexical-scope resolution of an identifier in a namespace without finalization or ignored bindings. It explicitly calls `Resolver::resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`.
Resolves an identifier in the current lexical scope with configurable finalization and optional binding suppression. It explicitly calls `Resolver::resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`.
Resolves a path against the current parent scope and rib stacks, optionally in a specific namespace and finalize mode. It explicitly calls `Resolver::resolve_path_with_ribs`.
Runs a closure inside a temporary namespace rib, pushing a new rib before execution and popping it afterward. It explicitly calls `Rib::new` around the provided `work` closure.

Executes work in the module scope for a node when that node defines a module, temporarily switching `parent_scope.module` and pushing module ribs for both value and type namespaces. It explicitly calls `get_module`, `replace`, `with_rib`, and then the supplied closure `f`.

Resolves generic parameter declarations while enforcing forward-reference bans for later type/const parameters and optionally `Self` in ADT defaults. Inside `with_lifetime_rib`, it explicitly calls `visit_param_bound` for bounds, `visit_ty` for type defaults, and `resolve_anon_const` for const defaults, while pushing and removing temporary ban ribs as parameters become available.
Runs a closure inside a temporary lifetime rib, saving and restoring lifetime-elision candidates around the work. It explicitly calls `LifetimeRib::new` around the provided `work` closure.

Resolves a named or anonymous lifetime use by handling `'static`, delegating `_` to `resolve_anonymous_lifetime`, and otherwise searching lifetime ribs from innermost to outermost. On success it explicitly calls `record_lifetime_res`; on special error cases it emits diagnostics such as forbidden non-static or undeclared lifetime errors.

Resolves an underscore or elided lifetime according to the active lifetime ribs. It may create a fresh lifetime with `create_fresh_lifetime` and record it with `record_lifetime_res`, emit lints or errors for forbidden anonymous lifetimes, accumulate elision failures, or report missing lifetime specifiers via `report_missing_lifetime_specifiers`.

Creates a synthetic underscore lifetime for an elided lifetime position, records an anchor range for it, and resolves it as an anonymous lifetime. It explicitly calls `record_lifetime_res` and `resolve_anonymous_lifetime`.
Allocates a fresh synthetic lifetime parameter for an anonymous lifetime, records it, and stores it for later HIR lowering. It explicitly calls `record_lifetime_param`.

Resolves omitted lifetime arguments in path segments that refer to lifetime-parameterized types or traits. It explicitly calls `record_lifetime_res` to create anchor and inferred entries; depending on context it may call `create_fresh_lifetime`, emit diagnostics, buffer lints, or call `report_missing_lifetime_specifiers` when explicit lifetimes are required.

Records the resolved meaning of a lifetime node, panicking if the node was already resolved, and tracks elision candidates for named, fresh, or static lifetimes. It updates the resolution map directly and does not call other listed methods.
Records the resolved meaning of a lifetime parameter node, panicking on duplicate resolution. It updates the resolution map directly and does not call other listed methods.

Resolves the lifetimes of a function signature by first resolving parameter patterns and types, then resolving the return type under the appropriate elision rib, and finally reporting elision failures if needed. It explicitly calls `resolve_fn_params`, wraps return-type traversal in `with_lifetime_rib`, and may call `report_missing_lifetime_specifiers`.

Resolves function parameter patterns and types while computing the lifetime elision candidate for the signature. For each parameter it explicitly calls `with_lifetime_rib` to resolve patterns via `resolve_pattern`, then calls `visit_ty` to collect lifetime candidates, and finally uses `find_lifetime_for_self` when `self`-based elision may apply.

Searches a type for references of the form `&'a Self` (including implicit/desugared self forms) to identify elision candidates tied to `self`. It builds a local visitor whose `visit_ty` logic uses `is_self_ty`, then walks the type to collect matching lifetime resolutions.

Checks whether a type denotes `Self`, either as implicit self, an explicit self type parameter/alias, or the current impl self type. It reads the path resolution via `full_res` and performs no calls to other listed methods.

Visits a type while detecting `&Self` references and recording the resolved lifetime used by that reference; when the referenced inner type is `Self`, it uses `is_self_ty` and stores the lifetime resolution, then calls `visit::walk_ty` to continue traversing nested type structure.
Overrides expression visiting as a no-op so this visitor only inspects types and does not recurse into expressions.

Resolves a loop/block label by searching label ribs from innermost to outermost, adjusting macro-generated labels when crossing `MacroDefinition` ribs, and returning either the matching label or an error. It explicitly calls `is_label_valid_from_rib` to reject labels hidden behind barriers and `suggestion_for_label_in_rib` to collect typo suggestions.
Checks whether a resolved label is reachable from the current scope by scanning intervening label ribs for barriers. It explicitly calls `is_label_barrier` on each rib kind.

Resolves an enum/struct/union item by installing the current self item, generic-parameter scopes, and a `Self` type alias for the ADT, then traversing the item body. It explicitly calls `with_current_self_item`, `with_generic_param_rib`, `with_self_rib`, and `visit::walk_item`.

Checks `use` trees for imports that incorrectly refer to local variables or type parameters, emitting future-proofing diagnostics for such lexical-scope captures. For each relevant namespace it explicitly calls `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`, may call `resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope` to probe through an item binding, and recursively calls `future_proof_import` on nested imports.

Dispatches late resolution for each item kind, setting up the appropriate ribs, doc-link handling, and specialized resolution flow. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links` for most items, `with_generic_param_rib` plus `visit::walk_item` for type aliases and functions, `resolve_adt` for enums/structs/unions, `resolve_implementation` for impls, `with_self_rib`, `visit_generics`, and `resolve_trait_items` for traits, `with_scope` for trait aliases, `with_static_rib`, `with_lifetime_rib`, `visit_ty`, and `resolve_const_body` for statics/consts, and `future_proof_import` for nested-use imports.

Creates temporary type, value, and lifetime ribs for generic parameters, records their bindings, checks for duplicate names and lifetime shadowing, runs a nested resolution action, then tears the ribs down and reports lifetime uses. It explicitly calls `Rib::new`, `signal_lifetime_shadowing`, `record_lifetime_param`, `report_error`, `record_partial_res`, and `maybe_report_lifetime_uses`.
